epic.name: Upload an expense file
unverifiedAssumptions: Verify the status wording the service actually uses: the screen assumes a submitted file's status reads as Uploaded, Validating, Validation failed, Imported or Cancelled. Those five come from the requirements document, not from the API specification (which types the status as free text with no fixed list). If the real service words them differently, statuses will show up unstyled and the 'finished importing' notification may never fire.

Verify a file you have just submitted appears in the list: the upload call answers with a generic acknowledgement and no file identifier, so the screen finds your new file by re-reading the active file list. If the service does not list a freshly submitted file straight away, you would get a successful confirmation but see nothing appear.

Verify a real CSV is accepted by the real service: the upload sends the setting, the setting name and the file name in the address and the file's raw bytes as the request body, exactly as the API specification describes. If the running service actually expects a form-style upload instead, every automated test still passes while real uploads are refused.
